summary: Eldorado NF lookout in El Dorado County; a 1929 item has a forest fire-guard couple posted there; FFLOS says Abandoned, map tags say destroyed; no source describes the site now.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Eldorado National Forest
facts.status_note: FFLOS lists it Abandoned; OpenStreetMap tags the point building:destroyed yes; a peak list calls it an LO site. Sources do not describe what remains.

events.note: William Littlefield, a fire guard on the Eldorado National Forest staff, and his new wife Alma were stationed at Plummer Lookout for the summer

corrections.why: The FFLOS California list types Plummer Ridge as Tree. The OpenStreetMap point is tagged man_made=tower, which is a generic tag.

notes_for_editor: Coordinates disagree: the brief point (38.6122946, -120.4477204, from OpenStreetMap) and FFLOS (38.62991, -120.38012) are about six km apart. The story says so and does not pick one. Status disagrees too: the brief says gone, FFLOS says Abandoned; the story keeps gone because the OSM tag and the peak-list LO site point the same way. Only one dated item was on the Forest Lookouts page (1929). A 2019 Eldorado NF lookout booklet on docslib names Plummer Lookout only in a garbled line, so it is not cited. Newspaper archives (The Mountain Democrat, via CDNC) were not searched; they could add construction and removal dates. Budget: 2 searches, 4 page reads.
